_notes.what: TEMPLATE for the machine-local config. Copy it to config/local.json (the init skill offers to do this on first run) and fill only the keys your run actually needs. local.json is machine-local and gitignored, it is the ONLY place a host path, an account id, or a tool location lives. No key ever ships with a filled value: a foreign default is worse than a named miss.
_notes.why: Nothing in this plugin embeds one operator's machine layout or one company's identifiers. Skills, scripts, and config reference values as ${local:<key>} and resolve them at run time.
resolution_order: 1. Environment variable, the key uppercased, dots and dashes to underscores, prefixed PM_LOCAL_ (e.g. ${local:tools_dir} reads PM_LOCAL_TOOLS_DIR).
2. config/local.json, the same dotted key under "local".

3. NAMED MISS, the run says which key is unset, what it would have unlocked, and offers to fill it. It never guesses, never substitutes another operator's value, and never renders a foreign default in your output.
rules: Keys hold POINTERS and IDENTIFIERS, never secret values: a path to a credential file, never the credential. Scripts test that a pointer resolves; they never read or echo the contents.
A missing key is a named MISS, not a crash: the affected capability is reported unavailable and the run continues on what it can prove.

Every ${local:<key>} used anywhere in this package MUST appear in this template (a completeness test enforces it), so `local.template.json` doubles as the documentation of every host-specific value the engine can want.
eng_plugin is the ONLY handoff seam: unset (the default) = standalone mode, the engine still produces the full requirements package, just with no downstream engineering handoff and no seam preflight.

_doc.provenance_id: The label written into receipts, stamps, and ledger appends instead of a machine hostname and OS user. Pick anything you are happy to publish (a role, a workspace name). Unset = receipts say 'unattributed', which is honest, and never leaks a machine identity.
_doc.eng_plugin.name: Optional engineering-handoff adapter. The name of the downstream engineering plugin/toolchain that consumes handoff packages. Unset = STANDALONE MODE: no seam artifacts are shipped anywhere, and every verb says so plainly instead of pretending a downstream exists.
_doc.eng_plugin.surfaces_registry: Path to the downstream toolchain's surface/repo registry (read-only ground truth for surface names and repositories). The engine reads it; it never writes it. Unset with eng_plugin.name set = surfaces come from your own answers and are marked as unverified against a registry.
_doc.eng_plugin.seam_check_cmd: Optional command that verifies your engine<->downstream contract versions still match. Exit 0 = proceed. Unset = the handoff records that no seam verification was available (never a silent pass).
_doc.eng_plugin.handoff_dir: Directory the downstream toolchain picks packages up from. Unset = the package stays where the run wrote it and the handoff step prints the path for a human to move.
_doc.secrets_dir: RESERVED and user-extensible: a directory where YOUR credential files live. No shipped script or capability row reads this key today, it is declared so a row you add can build pointer paths from it instead of hardcoding a location. Contents are never read by this plugin either way.
_doc.credential_index: RESERVED and user-extensible: a path to your own index of which credential lives where. No shipped script or capability row reads this key today, it is declared so a row you add can point a MISS at your index instead of naming one fixed location.
_doc.tools_dir: RESERVED and user-extensible: a directory holding locally installed analytics/CLI binaries. No shipped capability row probes it today, it is the documented place to point one you add.
_doc.corpus_base: Root of your read-only evidence corpora (research archives, prior-cycle outputs, exports). Pack pointers resolve against it.
_doc.harness_configs: Array of additional agent harnesses to inventory on this host, each {"id": "<label>", "format": "json"|"toml", "path": "<config file>", "servers_key": "<dotted key holding the tool/server table>"}. Empty/unset = only the default harness is inventoried, reported as a named limit.
_doc.analytics_web.property_id.prod: Web-analytics property/site id for PRODUCTION. Ids are per-call arguments, never baked into a skill file.
_doc.analytics_web.property_id.staging: Web-analytics property/site id for STAGING. Keeping both named is what stops a staging read being reported as a production fact.
_doc.analytics_web.service_account_json: Path to the read-only service-account credential file your web-analytics client uses.
_doc.analytics_product.project_id.prod: Product-analytics project id for PRODUCTION. Required explicitly on every production read (an unnamed project silently answers from the other one, the single most common wrong-answer source).
_doc.analytics_product.cli_config: Path to your product-analytics CLI config/profile file.
_doc.session_replay.token_path: Path to the session-replay export token file (pointer only).
_doc.session_replay.daily_query_budget: Integer: how many dashboard queries per day your plan allows. The verify verb enumerates its queries before the first call when this is set.
_doc.tag_container.id: RESERVED and user-extensible: a tag-manager container id, for when web instrumentation planning is in scope. No shipped script or capability row reads this key today.
_doc.issue_tracker.enabled: ELICITED, and the switch the other three keys hang off. This integration does not exist until the setup wizard asks for it and you answer yes; nothing here is preconfigured for any particular tracker or any particular company. Unset or false = the integration is ABSENT: no capability row is probed, no fix is printed, and nothing is named as missing, declining is a complete answer, not a gap. Set true only via the wizard's question, which also fills the three keys below.
_doc.issue_tracker.base_url: Base URL of YOUR issue tracker (the workspace root you would type into a browser). Recorded only after you say yes to the integration. Used to build read-only item-type requests; never written to.
_doc.issue_tracker.project_key: Project key inside that tracker whose stories and tickets may be read for backlog cross-checks. One project, named explicitly, so a cross-check can never quietly answer from a different backlog.
_doc.issue_tracker.auth_pointer: PATH TO the file holding your read-only API credential, a POINTER, never the credential itself. The token VALUE is never stored in config, never read by this plugin, and never echoed: probes test only that the pointer resolves to a readable file. If your harness already holds the credential, point this at that harness's credential file rather than copying the secret anywhere new.
_doc.docs_workspace.name: Docs/wiki workspace whose pages may be cited as evidence.
_doc.design_tool.token_path: Path to the design-tool access token file (pointer only) for design-parity reads.
_doc.packs_dir_extra: Extra directory scanned for context packs, so your own packs live outside this plugin and survive upgrades.
